resources.string: This page does two things: how the glass looks, and whether it is actually working right now. Changes apply immediately, no restart needed.
Turn this off and every panel snaps back to how it was, with zero effect on launching games. This is the only master switch; everything below obeys it.
Decides which panels get glass at all. Small buttons and thin dividers only show a ring of noise and cost performance for nothing, so only big enough panels qualify.
Big pieces only: nav bar, bottom action bar, whole cards. Cheapest, and looks good enough.
Medium panels too: list rows, input boxes, small cards. Prettier, noticeably heavier on battery. If the phone gets hot or laggy, switch back to Light.
How wide the distorted ring is. Too narrow reads as an outline; too wide looks like the whole panel is smeared. This also caps the displacement, the two are tied together.

How far the picture along the edge gets pushed. Too small and nothing moves, which looks like there is no effect at all; too large and the edge folds into stripes. The default 2.2x is visible without folding.
Displacement is currently %s x the band width

This ratio is identical on every phone and every panel size. If it ever changes with panel size, that is a bug, and it is exactly how the previous version broke: on one phone a small panel got 0.55x (nothing moved) while a full screen panel got 10.7x (folded into stripes).

Android 13 and up use real refraction (Snell + dispersion + Fresnel). Below that the capability does not exist, so an approximation is used and the look is one tier weaker. That is a system limit, not a misconfiguration.
How many panels on screen currently have glass. This number changes as you switch pages, which is normal.
The glass samples this blurred image, which is why refraction reads as glass instead of a shifted picture. If it is missing the original image is used automatically: worse, but silent.
Goes up by one on every wallpaper change. Glass uses it to decide whether to rebind its texture; if it stops moving, wallpaper changes are not being announced.
Use this after changing wallpaper or when some panel looks like it never got glass. It walks the whole tree again looking for panels that qualify.
Puts the status above into the clipboard as plain text. When something breaks, paste it straight to me instead of hunting through folders.
Band 22dp, displacement 2.2x, coverage Light. Press this when things get tangled; no need to reinstall.
